text:
Cole Knuble got his first NHL goal on Wednesday night in Buffalo, then added a second in the third period, and Philadelphia beat the Sabres 3-1 for its third straight win. Knuble's first came at 14:49 of the opening period, a backhand with help from Oliver Bonk and Denver Barkey. Trevor Zegras made it 2-0 with a power-play goal in the last minute of the period, and Knuble's wrist shot early in the third made it 3-1.

The scoreboard hid a game Buffalo mostly controlled in the chances. The Sabres out-chanced Philadelphia 1.88 to 0.98 in expected goals (a measure of the quality of the shots each side took) in the first period, and finished the night at 4.12 to 3.97. By the same measure, the Sabres deserved to win slightly more often than not: 52 percent of simulated replays of every shot went their way. What separated the teams was Dan Vladar. He stopped 27 of 28 shots and saved 3.1 goals more than the quality of those shots would normally allow. The best chance he turned away was a 36 percent look for Jason Zucker in the third.

Zucker did beat him once, deflecting in a power-play goal with 35 seconds left in the second to make it 2-1. Buffalo took 25 penalty minutes to Philadelphia's 11, and went 1 for 3 on the power play while the Flyers went 1 for 5. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen allowed three goals on 26 shots, and the 3.97 expected goals against him suggests he was not the problem. Philadelphia leaves with a three-game winning streak. The Sabres will look for a way to turn the better chances into goals.
